newsitem.title: CHINA: Honda plans to boost China motorbike output.
newsitem.headline: Honda plans to boost China motorbike output.

text.p: Japan's Honda Motor Co Ltd will boost output and product quality at its motorcycle plants in China to try to stay on top of the fiercely competitive market, a company official said on Friday.
Honda's three motorbike joint ventures in China made more than 360,000 units in 1996, out of a total nationwide production of 9.3 million, said Sachi Itoh, spokeswoman for Honda's China operations.
"Boosting output at our joint ventures is something we are working hard at," Itoh said but declined to give details of the firm's production plans.

Motorcycle output has soared in China over the last few years and the growth trend is expected to continue as more people seek a relatively cheap and quick means of transport, Itoh said in an interview.
"With the improvement of Chinese people's living standards, production is increasing," she said.
Official figures show the sector had an output capacity of 20 million units a year and Itoh said China currently has more than 140 motorcycle and scooter manufacturers.
These makers have struggled to turn profits as inventories rise and manufacturers slash prices to try to boost market share.
"Competition in the Chinese motorcycle industry is really fierce," Itoh said, adding that Honda will focus on product quality and after-sales service to stay competitive.
Honda has motorcycle joint ventures in the cities of Tianjin, Chongqing and Guangzhou. Company officials have said Honda is not currently looking for new partners in the sector.
